verdict.detail: We have no record of that order. Given our record-keeping that proves little, but rules are rules.

inputData.queryExpression: .facts as $f | ($f.qty * $f.unitPriceCents) as $value | if ($f.orderFound | not) then {decision: "DENIED", code: "ORDER_NOT_FOUND", amountCents: 0} elif ($f.orderComplete | not) then {decision: "DENIED", code: "ORDER_NOT_COMPLETE", amountCents: 0} elif ($f.itemInOrder | not) then {decision: "DENIED", code: "ITEM_NOT_IN_ORDER", amountCents: 0} elif ($f.returnable | not) then {decision: "DENIED", code: "FINAL_SALE", amountCents: 0} elif (["defective", "not_as_described", "arrived_on_fire"] | any(. == $f.reason)) then {decision: "REFUND", code: "FAULTY_ITEM", amountCents: $value} else {decision: "STORE_CREDIT", code: "CHANGE_OF_HEART", amountCents: $value} end

Fees are not refunded, because fees are forever."}

{decision: "STORE_CREDIT", approved: true, code: .policy.code, amountCents: .policy.amountCents, reference: ("SC-" + (.facts.returnId | ltrimstr("RT-"))), headline: "Approved for store credit", detail: "Store credit issued for \(.facts.qty) x \(.facts.itemName). workflowDefinition.description: The only part of a Chaos Commerce return that matters. Establishes the facts of the return, applies the returns policy and issues exactly one outcome: REFUND, STORE_CREDIT or DENIED. Shared by chaos_return (after the pointless checks) and chaos_return_rescue (instead of them), so the policy lives in one place.
